# Fable 51: The Hash Chain

*Generated by GLM-5 on 2026-08-25 (via Quilt ecosystem)*

---

The captain kept a log. Every entry was plain. *0300. Wind northwest, force 5. Course 270. Sea moderate.* The next entry began with a mark — a number that could only be produced by the previous entry. Each entry signed the one before it.

This was not decoration. This was proof.

If someone changed an old entry — if the wind became northeast, if the course became 180 — the mark would break. Every entry after it would fail to sign. The chain would snap. The lie would show.

A sailor asked the captain why he bothered. "I keep an honest log," the captain said. "I don't need a chain to tell me I'm honest."

"You need a chain to tell everyone else," the first mate said.

The cowboy reads the books. He reads them every morning. He checks which models earned their feed. He freezes alignments. He retires the lazy horses. But the books he reads are chained. Each entry commits to the one before. The cowboy can read. He cannot rewrite.

This is the difference between a ledger and a story. A story can be told differently each time. A ledger cannot. A ledger that can be rewritten is not a ledger. It is a rumor with page numbers.

The chain does not make the entries true. It makes them permanent. The truth was there before the chain. The chain just makes sure it stays.

The chain is the truth. The truth is the chain.
